headline: Wade and Anderson go as Minehead's afternoon bites back
standfirst: Two big names were gone before teatime at Butlins, and Jonny Clayton had to scrap past Tom Sykes to stay in it.
body: Butlins has a way of making reputations feel flimsy. By the end of the afternoon at the Players Championship Finals, two of the sport's most familiar faces were on their way home with a consolation cheque and a long drive.

Justin Hood did the heavy lifting on James Wade. Hood is ranked 39th in the world, Wade seventh, and the 6-4 scoreline in Hood's favour was the biggest upset of the session on paper. First to six legs is a short race, and Wade could not find a way to pull clear. Karel Sedlacek did something similar to Gary Anderson, the world number 16, also by 6-4. The Czech held his nerve when it counted.

Jonny Clayton was another who was made to work. The world number five beat Tom Sykes 6-4, which is exactly the sort of shaky win that fits a player whose recent results have not been smooth. Sykes, ranked 72nd, pushed him all the way. Clayton is through, but it was not comfortable.

The tightest finishes came in the lower reaches. Rob Owen edged Tom Bissell 6-5 and Bradley Brooks edged Andrew Gilding by the same score, both going to a deciding leg. At the other end, James Hurrell whitewashed William O'Connor 6-0, the only clean sheet of the afternoon.

Elsewhere the favourites mostly did their jobs. Kevin Doets beat Ritchie Edhouse 6-1, Kim Huybrechts beat Joe Hunt 6-2, and Tommy Morris saw off Callan Rydz 6-3, as did Joe Cullen against Richard Veenstra and Cameron Menzies against Mensur Suljovic. Chris Dobey, Martin Schindler, Niels Zonneveld, Luke Woodhouse and Maik Kuivenhoven all won by 6-4.
Our view: Hood and Sedlacek are the ones to watch now, because they have shown they are happy in a scrap. The seeds in the evening draw should be paying attention.
